question.prompt: A farmer monitoring an irrigation water tank records its depth, in centimetres, at the end of every hour, and notices the depth increases following a steady, repeating pattern: 14, 21, 28, 35, and so on, hour after hour, always increasing by 7 centimetres each time. If this exact pattern keeps continuing at that same steady rate without changing, what will the tank's recorded depth be after the 8th hour?

visuals.altText: Line graph of tank depth over the first four hours: 14, 21, 28 and 35 centimetres.

question.explanation: Each recorded depth is 7 centimetres more than the depth recorded immediately before it, so the depth increases at a steady rate of 7 centimetres every hour. Starting from 14 centimetres at hour 1, reaching hour 8 requires 7 further hours of steady increase. Multiplying 7 centimetres by those 7 extra hours gives a total increase of 49 centimetres from the starting depth. Adding 49 centimetres to 14 centimetres gives a final depth of 63 centimetres after the 8th hour.
